defect: Automatic remote mutation retry bounded replay only inside one call; independent concurrent/periodic callers did not share provider 429/Retry-After cooldown.
impact: Repeated callers could hammer a throttled provider despite individually safe retry loops.
negative_invariant: Cooldown is canonical-action scoped, bounded, secret-free, cancellable, and does not replay single-attempt side effects.

defect: DoH HTTP cache inserted arbitrary upstream responses, including transient 5xx failures, as cached DNS values.
impact: A temporary upstream failure could be amplified as a cached answer failure.
negative_invariant: Only non-empty HTTP 200 DNS-message responses enter fresh cache authority.

defect: Multiple DNS caches were unbounded and DoH cache eviction used a maintenance goroutine without cancellation ownership.
impact: Untrusted/high-cardinality DNS keys could grow process memory and maintenance could outlive service cancellation.
negative_invariant: DNS cache entry counts are hard bounded and maintenance stops with context cancellation.

defect: Concurrent same-key DoH misses could fan out to duplicate upstream refreshes; GET dns query input was not rejected before decode/upstream work.
impact: Cache stampedes and malformed/oversized keys could multiply external work or allocation.
negative_invariant: One same-key refresh is in flight and invalid/oversized wire keys fail before upstream work.

defect: Weighted DoH proxy used an unbounded map, a rand.Rand without synchronization, and assumed a non-empty provider set.
impact: Memory growth, data races, or panic could occur under concurrent selection/configuration edge cases.
negative_invariant: Proxy cache is bounded, RNG access is serialized, non-positive weights are ignored, and no-provider state returns an error.

defect: Failover DoH resolver provider/client configuration could be mutated while resolution read it, and ClearProviders could leave selection paths indexing an empty slice.
impact: Concurrent reconfiguration could race; empty provider state could panic rather than fail closed.
negative_invariant: Provider lists are snapshot-read, empty provider state fails closed, and HTTP client reconfiguration replaces snapshots rather than mutating in-flight clients.

defect: Process readiness could erase restart debt immediately; a later audit also found expired failure history was only pruned before restart delay, not when recording/evaluating a failure after a long healthy run.
impact: Ready-then-crash loops could avoid escalating backoff, while stale historical failures could falsely trip the circuit breaker after prolonged health.
negative_invariant: Only a stable-ready interval resets consecutive backoff debt; rolling history remains independent and is time-window-pruned at every decision boundary.
